stem.text: Let f be the function defined by \( f(x) = \begin{cases} \frac{2 x^{2} - 5 x + 3}{x - 1}, & x \ne 1 \\ -1, & x = 1 \end{cases} \). Determine whether f is continuous at \( x = 1 \), and justify your answer.

answer_key.label: f is continuous at \( x = 1 \), because the limit of f(x) there is -1, which equals f(1).

worked_solution.text: The function value at the boundary is \( f(1) = -1 \), from the second line of the rule.
worked_solution.rule_named: evaluate the function at the input

worked_solution.text: For \( x \ne 1 \) the quotient simplifies to \( 2 x - 3 \), so \( \lim_{x \to 1} f(x) = -1 \) from both sides.
The limit equals the function value, so f is continuous at \( x = 1 \).
worked_solution.rule_named: the limit must equal the function value

options.label: f is not continuous at \( x = 1 \), because the quotient gives 0/0 at \( x = 1 \), so f(1) is undefined.
options.derivation: x = 1 substituted into the quotient, which applies only for x not equal to 1, giving 0/0

options.label: f is continuous at \( x = 1 \), because the limit of f(x) there is -1, which equals f(1).
f is continuous at \( x = 1 \), because the limits from both sides are -1, and matching one sided limits alone make a function continuous.
options.derivation: continuity concluded from the agreement of the one sided limits, with the function value never compared

options.label: f is continuous at \( x = 1 \), because f(1) = -1 is defined, and a function is continuous wherever it has a value.
options.derivation: continuity concluded because the function has a value at the input
